text:
Tom Wilson scored 30 goals last season. He has two through 19 games this year and none in his last 15, on 4.4 expected goals (the quality of chances) over that stretch. Our numbers say he's due: two goals on 5.9 expected for the season, and he's still getting to the dangerous spots.

The month also brought a familiar controversy. On Nov. 7 against Florida, Wilson was ejected after barely two minutes of ice time for boarding Sandis Vilmanis, who was hurt on the play. He told RMNB, "I was trying to make a north-south hit," and the league didn't suspend him, a ruling Florida Hockey Now called wrong.

The rest of his game holds up. At five on five Washington has taken 53% of the expected goals with him on, and Evolving-Hockey had him in the 99th percentile among forwards at taking chances away last season, worth 1.9 wins overall. His ice time is down about a minute and a half a night lately, and the Capitals have lost three straight. Our numbers read the slump as mostly finishing, with a few fewer chances mixed in.
